findings.reason: TrieUtils.ts:45 declares `index: number`, but lines 54-60 branch on `typeof index !== 'number'` and compare `'' + uint32Index !== index`, which only makes sense for string keys passed by JS callers. Runtime is unchanged because callers are .js, so the type is wrong but harmless today; low.
findings.claim: wrapIndex types index as number while its body handles string indices, hiding that branch from the type checker.
findings.evidence: Line 45 has `index: number`, yet lines 54-59 run `if (typeof index !== 'number') { const uint32Index = index >>> 0; if ('' + uint32Index !== index ...` and narrow `index` to `never`. JS callers such as List.js:71, Seq.js:166 and CollectionImpl.js:610 pass the user-supplied key through unchanged. Runtime is unchanged because the callers are .js, but a future TS caller passing a string key would be wrongly rejected, and edits inside the branch would not be checked.

findings.reason: wholeSlice (TrieUtils.ts:68-73) checks `end === undefined` and `size !== undefined`, resolveIndex checks `index === undefined`/`size === undefined`, and SetRef guards `if (ref)`. JS callers such as Range.js:77 and Map.js:216 can pass undefined, so the required-number/Ref types misstate the contract. There is no runtime effect, so it stays low.
findings.claim: Signatures declare required number/Ref params that bodies test for undefined and callers pass undefined.
findings.evidence: `wholeSlice(begin: number, end: number, size: number)` checks `end === undefined` and `size !== undefined`. `resolveIndex(index: number, size: number, ...)` checks `index === undefined` and `size === undefined`. `SetRef(ref: Ref)` guards `if (ref)`. Callers like Range.js:77 `wholeSlice(begin, end, this.size)` from `slice(begin, end)` pass an undefined `end`, and Map.js:216 `SetRef(didChangeSize)` can pass an undefined ref. Optional or `| undefined` types would describe this correctly.

findings.reason: TrieUtils.ts:34, 36 and 39 add three `@ts-expect-error` comments in ensureSize because `iter` is typed as the public Collection, which has no `size`/`__iterate`. The errors are suppressed, not fixed. This is a typing-quality concern only; low.
findings.claim: New @ts-expect-error suppressions silence type errors instead of typing iter correctly.
findings.evidence: ensureSize has `// @ts-expect-error size should exists on Collection` at lines 34 and 39, and `// @ts-expect-error size should exists on Collection, __iterate does exist on Collection` at line 36. The parameter is typed `Collection<unknown, unknown>` even though the function reads and writes internal `size` and calls `__iterate`.

findings.reason: diff.patch changes four comments in src/utils/deepEqual.ts from 'size exists' to 'size should exists'. The edit is wording only and outside the TrieUtils conversion, and it adds a grammar error. It has no behavioural effect; low.
findings.claim: Unrelated comment-only edits in deepEqual.ts introduce a grammar error.
findings.evidence: Four hunks change `// @ts-expect-error size exists on Collection` to `// @ts-expect-error size should exists on Collection` (lines 22, 38, 60, 94). This is wording only, with no behaviour change, in a file the conversion did not need to touch.
